title: Diego Hurtado de Mendoza (imperial ambassador in Rome) → Ferrante Gonzaga, letter with enclosures partly in cipher
correspondents: Diego Hurtado de Mendoza → Ferrante Gonzaga
shelfmark: Biblioteca Estense Universitaria, Modena, Autografoteca Campori, Lettera H, Hurtado de Mendoza, Diego, sfasc. I, cc. 40-46
folio_note: 14 canvases; enclosures cc. 42-44 with lines of symbol cipher and a list of names (possibly a partial key or a clear summary).
status: Record: 'Le cc. 42-44 contengono allegati alla lettera, alcuni cifrati.' Hurtado de Mendoza appears in Dan's repo for other archives, not for this item. The other ~95 Hurtado de Mendoza records here were checked: none mentions cipher. Manifest uuid(s): e02077fa-33a9-4749-b581-f88f2d45e9be. Compare with the Hurtado de Mendoza key of open PR #216 (mendoza1548), same sender a year earlier; not tested.
why: Charles V's ambassador in Rome writing to the governor of Milan during the Parma-Piacenza crisis of 1549.
verify: Read the list on c. 43 at full size: if it pairs names with signs, it is a key.

title: 'Francesco Rota' → 'Mr. Vatron' in London, The Hague 8 Apr 1624, written by Ludwig Camerarius, mostly in cipher
shelfmark: Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 10398 (Collectio Camerariana vol. 48), n. 106
status: Halm, Verzeichniss der handschriftlichen Sammlung der Camerarii (1874), p. 95: "Lettera di Francesco Rota à Mr. Vatron à Londre, Haia 8 Apr. 1624 (von Lud. Cam. geschrieben, grossentheils in Chiffern)". Cover names: n. 107 is 'Francesco Rota al Sign. Lod. Camerario, Bruxelles 29 Apr.', so 'Rota' is a cover used in this channel. Mostly cipher; Italian plaintext. Not on DECODE (repo dumps have no BSB Clm 103xx). Image: https://www.digitale-sammlungen.de/en/view/bsb00116447?page=1 (IIIF https://api.digitale-sammlungen.de/iiif/presentation/v2/bsb00116447/manifest). Viewed by WAINUT on 3 Nov 2026 (scan 469): Italian clear text with run-together two-digit numbers and the letters g, p, t, c, x and & as code signs; no decipherment on the page, so ciphertext-only. Names the Capuchin Giacinto ('Non erubesco Evangelium', cf. n. 108). Not the code of Camerarius's 1621-22 letters to Solms (WAINUT's separate camerarius1621 submission). Not attempted.
why: A covert Palatine channel to London in 1624, the year of the Anglo-Dutch-Palatine alliance talks, run under cover names.
score_note: Scored from Halm's catalogue entry during the Nov 2026 bavarikon/BSB sweep (research/wainut_leads_2026-11-03/); the volume's scans are confirmed online (MDZ, from microfilm, legible), the cipher leaves not yet located in them
verify: Transcribe scan 469 in two passes; look for other 'Rota' pieces (n. 107, n. 108) that may carry the same system with glosses.

seen.where: MDZ bsb00116447 scan 469 (Clm 10398, fol. 233, piece number 106), read at 1418 px. Scan 470, the verso, is blank; scan 471 is n. 107.
seen.extent: One page, about 26 lines of letter, with code on most lines up to the close (about 20 lines). Not counted by machine; no transcription made.
seen.cipher: Italian clear text with runs of two-digit numbers ('21 10 22 x 49', '94 40 20', '50 30 90') and the signs g, p, t, c, x, r, n and & mixed in with numbers ('g 34', 'g 27', 'c 94'). Nothing is written over or beside any group: no decipherment on the leaf. Dated 'Haia 8 Aprile 1624', signed 'Fran.co Rota', addressed 'A Monsieur Monsieur Vatron Londre'.

Camerariana XLVIII n. 108, summarises n. 107 and n. 110, quotes n. 111, but has no Vatron and does not cite n. 106. Söltl, Religionskrieg (archive.org derreligionskri01slgoog) searched in full text: a dated account records Rota at The Hague, March-April 1624, no Vatron. prior_art.literature: Gardiner, History of England V ch. XLVII and Krüner, Johann von Rusdorf (1876) describe the mission without this letter. Schubert, Ludwig Camerarius (1955/2013) is not online and was not seen. Searches on Rota, Vatron and cipher found no decipherment.

earlier_block.key_check: camerarius1621 key.tsv does not fit: its code is German and one-part, with groups up to about 3200, while this letter uses two-digit numbers and letter signs in Italian. Not attempted. Goetz cites Hyacinth and Alexander reports in cipher ('Chiffr. Or./Abschr.', Munich St.A. K. schw. 442/19), an untested possible route to the same family; no key found on record.

title: Anselm Casimir, Elector of Mainz, and Ferdinand, Elector of Cologne → Gottfried Huyn von Geleen, 22 Oct 1633, in cipher (original)
correspondents: Anselm Casimir Wambold von Umstadt (Elector of Mainz) and Ferdinand of Bavaria (Elector of Cologne) → Gottfried Huyn von Geleen (Catholic League general)
shelfmark: Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 10406 (Collectio Camerariana vol. 56), n. 206
folio_note: Halm 1874 numbers the pieces (n. 206), not folios; the whole volume is scanned on MDZ.
status: Halm, Verzeichniss der handschriftlichen Sammlung der Camerarii (1874), p. 134: "Anselm Casimir Churf. zu Mainz und Ferdinand Churf. zu Cöln an Gottl. Guyn de Geelen, 22 Oct. 1633 (in Chiffern). Original". An original letter of two Catholic electors to a League general, so presumably intercepted by the Swedish side and passed to Camerarius; no decipherment noted. Not on DECODE (repo dumps have no BSB Clm 103xx). Image: https://www.digitale-sammlungen.de/en/view/bsb00116454?page=1 (IIIF https://api.digitale-sammlungen.de/iiif/presentation/v2/bsb00116454/manifest).
why: Intercepted Catholic League military correspondence from the Westphalian campaign of 1633; would show what the League planned and whether the Swedes could read it.

earlier_block.note: Corrections: lead's shelfmark and MDZ links point to Clm 10416 / bsb00116464, the wrong volume. Salutation 'Rme Illme Princeps' and closing 'Rmae et Illmae Celsitudinis Vrae' are clear; dated 'Raptissime Osnabrugi 1633. 13 Aug.'; signed with initials I read as C. L. The address names a reverend prince, not an elector as such: Bishop Wartenberg, who had left for Bonn, is as possible as Elector Ferdinand. Faint marks over two lines look like show-through; check at colour resolution. Forst's Wartenberg correspondence ends 1631 from memory, not opened. Searches run: Osnabrück 13 Aug 1633 cipher; Clm 10415 + Chiffern; Bierther volume. None found a decipherment. No key tested.
